title: Reversible Primitive–Composition Alignment for Continual Vision–Language Learning
claim: Under sequential adaptation, primitive skills stay stable while compositional ability steadily decays, and naive fine-tuning degrades most.
layout: 3 panels in a row, shared x-axis task index, line plots with bands
description: Three side-by-side line plots share the x-axis, task index 1 to 6. Each plot shows three methods: FT in orange, EWC in blue, and Replay-Text in green. Shaded bands show 95% confidence intervals. Panel (a) plots composition accuracy, which falls from about 0.89 to 0.65 for FT, 0.73 for EWC and 0.79 for Replay-Text. Panel (b) plots CRR, a retention ratio that starts at 1.0 and falls to about 0.80 for FT and 0.93 for Replay-Text. Panel (c) plots zero-shot composition accuracy on unseen pairs, which drops most steeply, with FT reaching about 0.48. Method names label the line ends and also appear in a bottom legend. The eye goes to the steep orange line diverging below the others. Captions sit below each panel.
caption: Exploratory curves with error bands. Primitives are stable; composition degrades with task index, most for FT.
abstract: Vision-language (VL) models are increasingly deployed in non-stationary settings, yet under sequential adaptation they often preserve primitive recognition while losing compositional structure, especially with tight rehearsal budgets and no task IDs. We address this gap by asking how a continual VL system can maintain structurally dependable behaviour while safeguarding zero-shot performance. We introduce Compo-ReAlign, a structure-first recipe built around three components: a reversible composer that maps primitive embeddings to compositions by design, a multi-positive InfoNCE that jointly aligns textual and composed views of the same target, and a spectral trust region that clips updates when alignment sensitivity inflates. Across compositional DIL and multi-domain MTIL retrieval, Compo-ReAlign sets a new state of the art, improves over the strongest prior by +2.4 R@1, and reduces forgetting by 40%. We provide a compact, reversible alignment head with geometry-aware training for compositionally robust VL continual learning.
